cues.en: One of the things I really like about Amsterdam is the shops and restaurants that are dotted throughout residential areas in the city.
cues.zh: 阿姆斯特丹我最喜欢的特色之一，就是散布在全市各个居民区的商店和餐馆。

cues.en: These patios and local shops provide a lot of interesting destinations that are always within a very short walk or bicycle ride. This
cues.zh: 这些露台和本地小店提供了很多有趣的去处，步行或骑自行车片刻即可到达。这

cues.en: is different from a high street or main street where the shops are all along one major street.
cues.zh: 与那种所有店铺都挤在一条主街上的商业街截然不同。

cues.en: Cities in The Netherlands, like most countries, have high streets too. But these retail pockets bring an interesting character and liveliness to residential neighborhoods and are a more quiet and enjoyable environment to sit in or shop in than along a busy main street.
cues.zh: 和大多数国家一样，荷兰的城市也有商业街。但这些零售小聚落给居民区带来了独特的气质和活力，比喧闹的主街更安静、更适合坐下来休憩或购物。

cues.en: In many ways, these pockets of retail and restaurants remind me of the alleyways of Taipei,
cues.zh: 在很多方面，这些零售和餐馆聚集区让我想起了台北的小巷，

cues.en: which were my favorite part of the city as they provided liveliness while also making what would otherwise be a dark alley into a location that was inviting and interesting.
cues.zh: 那曾是我最喜欢的部分，它们既充满了生机，又把原本可能阴暗的小巷变成了一个温馨有趣的地方。

cues.en: So these pockets of shops and restaurants are in no way unique to The Netherlands.
cues.zh: 所以，这种密集的商店和餐馆并非荷兰独有。

cues.en: But what is interesting is that they are illegal to build in almost all of The US and Canada.
cues.zh: 但有趣的是，在几乎整个美国和加拿大，建造它们都是非法的。

cues.en: North American cities follow an approach called Euclidean zoning.
cues.zh: 北美城市采用了一种叫做欧几里得区划的方法。

cues.en: If you've ever played SimCity or Skylines,
cues.zh: 如果你玩过《模拟城市》或《都市：天际线》，

cues.en: this will be familiar to you.
cues.zh: 你对这个概念就不会陌生。

cues.en: Euclidean zoning will come up in future videos because it's a big source of problems with North American city design, but I'm not going to go into too much detail of the history here.
cues.zh: 欧几里得区划会在以后的视频中详细讨论，因为它是北美城市设计中许多问题的根源，但我在这里就不多讲它的历史了。

cues.en: If you want to learn more,
cues.zh: 如果你想了解更多，

cues.en: the exceptional urban planning channel City Beautiful has made some good quality videos about zoning in US cities. I'll put links below.
cues.zh: 优秀的城市规划频道 City Beautiful 制作了一些关于美国城市分区规划的高质量视频，我把链接放在下方。

cues.en: But for our purposes now, here's the quick summary.
cues.zh: 但就我们目前的目的而言，以下是简要总结。

cues.en: During the industrial revolution,
cues.zh: 在工业革命期间，

cues.en: cities were pretty horrible places. Someone could literally open a steel mill in the middle of a residential neighborhood
cues.zh: 城市是非常糟糕的地方。有人甚至可以直接在居民区中间开办一家钢铁厂，

cues.en: and this led to horrible pollution and a terrible living environment.
cues.zh: 这导致了可怕的污染和恶劣的生活环境。

cues.en: So zoning was introduced to separate incompatible land uses.
cues.zh: 于是引入了分区规划，以分隔不兼容的土地用途。

cues.en: This was probably the single most significant contribution
cues.zh: 这可能是城市规划师在职业历史上对公共卫生做出的最具意义的贡献，

cues.en: that urban planners made to public health in the history of the profession and likely saved millions of lives,
cues.zh: 并且很可能拯救了数百万人的生命，

cues.en: which is why almost every country has some kind of zoning ordinances.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么几乎每个国家都有某种分区条例。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: some countries took this a step too far and decided that absolutely everything should be separated from absolutely everything else.
cues.zh: 一些国家在这条路上走得太远，认为绝对所有东西都应该彼此完全隔离开来。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: means that in most North American cities, if an area is zoned as residential,
cues.zh: 意味着在大多数北美城市，如果一个地区被划为住宅区，

cues.en: then literally nothing else can be built in that area.
cues.zh: 那么该地区内字面上将不允许建造任何其他东西。

cues.en: Here is a typical zoning map in this case of my hometown of London in Canada.
cues.zh: 这是一张典型的分区地图，以我的家乡加拿大伦敦市为例。

cues.en: It is illegal to open a shop or restaurant anywhere within the yellow shaded area.
cues.zh: 在黄色阴影区域内的任何地方开商店或餐馆都是非法的。

cues.en: Now admittedly,
cues.zh: 当然，

cues.en: it is important to keep a residential area quiet and comfortable to live in and that's not always compatible with other uses.
cues.zh: 保持住宅区安静和适宜居住是很重要的，而这并不总是与其他用途相容。

cues.en: In The Netherlands, there are sometimes issues with noise,
cues.zh: 在荷兰，有时会遇到噪音、

cues.en: crowds, garbage, and other problems related to living right next to or above a commercial property.
cues.zh: 人群、垃圾，以及其他紧邻或位于商业地产上方所带来的问题。

cues.en: But like all things in city planning, there is a balance to be achieved.
cues.zh: 但就像城市规划中的所有事情一样，这需要寻找一个平衡点。

cues.en: Modern North American planning takes a very extremist view that there is no value to having shops and restaurants within a residential neighborhood.
cues.zh: 现代北美规划采取了一种极端的观点，认为在住宅区内开设商店和餐厅没有任何价值。

cues.en: But North American zoning is extremist in general.
cues.zh: 但北美的区划（zoning）向来都很极端。

cues.en: For example, if a neighborhood is zoned r one for single family homes,
cues.zh: 例如，如果一个街区被划为只允许建独栋住宅的 R1 区，

cues.en: then nothing else, not even townhouses or apartments, can exist there.
cues.zh: 那么其他任何东西，哪怕是联排别墅或公寓，都不能在那里存在。

cues.en: I'll talk about that in more detail in the future,
cues.zh: 我以后会详细谈这一点，

cues.en: but in the meantime, you can watch the City Beautiful video, the case against single family zoning.
cues.zh: 但在此期间，你可以观看 City Beautiful 的视频，了解反对独栋住宅区划的理由。

cues.en: What's interesting to me is that this was not always the case. In our former neighborhood in Toronto, built about a hundred years ago, there were several commercial buildings built within the neighborhood.
cues.zh: 对我而言有趣的是，过去并非总是如此。在我们以前位于多伦多的街区，建于大约一百年前，社区里就有几栋商业建筑。

cues.en: These areas have been grandfathered into the zoning code and are some of the most desirable and expensive
cues.zh: 这些区域作为历史遗留被豁免于新的区划法，并成为整个城市中最抢手、最昂贵的

cues.en: neighborhoods in the whole city.
cues.zh: 街区。

cues.en: But despite their appeal,
cues.zh: 但尽管它们极具吸引力，

cues.en: new neighborhoods will never be built this way again.
cues.zh: 新的街区再也不会以这种方式建造了。

cues.en: Beyond the liveliness that these places bring to a neighborhood, the fundamental issue here is walkability.
cues.zh: 除了这些地方为街区带来的活力之外，这里根本的问题是步行便利性。

cues.en: If there's a local shop, grocer, restaurant or pub in your neighborhood,
cues.zh: 如果你的社区里有一家本地商店、杂货店、餐厅或酒吧，

cues.en: then you can walk there.
cues.zh: 那么你就可以步行前往。

cues.en: But if your residential neighborhood is separated from every other use, then it means you have to drive to do anything you want to do and so does everyone else.
cues.zh: 但是，如果你的住宅区与其他所有功能区完全隔离，那就意味着你干什么都得开车，其他人也一样。

cues.en: That results in a lot of car traffic because it doesn't matter if you're driving across town or just need to buy a bag of milk, you have to get in your car.
cues.zh: 这会导致大量的汽车交通，因为不管你是要横跨整个城镇，还是只想买一袋牛奶，你都必须上车。

cues.en: And yes, where I'm from, we buy milk in bags and we like it that way.
cues.zh: 没错，我老家买牛奶是用袋装的，而且我们就喜欢这样。

cues.en: And then pour a milk.
cues.zh: 然后再倒出来喝。

cues.en: But once you've gone to the trouble of getting into your car, you're much less likely to drive to several small shops.
cues.zh: 但既然你已经费劲上了车，你就不太可能再开车去好几家小店铺了。

cues.en: Meaning most people skip local businesses and drive to the power center with a giant parking lot.
cues.zh: 这意味着大多数人都会跳过本地商户，而是开车去带有巨大停车场的大型商业中心。

cues.en: Shops in walkable areas are more likely to be run by local entrepreneurs who contribute significantly to the local economy in a way that big box stores do not and I will talk about that in a future video about the twisted economics of big box stores in North America.
cues.zh: 步行区里的店铺更有可能由本地创业者经营，他们对地方经济的贡献是大型仓储超市无法比拟的，我会在未来关于北美大型仓储超市扭曲经济学的一期视频中探讨这一点。

cues.en: By comparison, a walkable neighborhood has enough people living within walking distance for small shops to stay in business and parking lots are not required
cues.zh: 相比之下，一个适合行走的街区有足够多的人口在步行范围内，足以让小店铺维持生计，并且不需要停车场，

cues.en: making space available for patios, parquettes and places for people to live.
cues.zh: 从而腾出空间来建造露台、微型公园以及供人们居住的场所。

cues.en: Thankfully there is a realization in many US and Canadian cities that Euclidean zoning has gone too far.
cues.zh: 谢天谢地，许多美国和加拿大的城市已经意识到，欧几里得式区划已经走得太远了。

cues.en: You'll hear urban planners talk about mixed use development which is what the rest of the world calls the way you build things.
cues.zh: 你会听到城市规划者谈论混合用途开发，也就是世界其他地方所称的正常建设方式。

cues.en: However, I find these developments are still highly localized such as at a transit hub or along an arterial road.
cues.zh: 然而，我发现这些发展仍然高度局限于交通枢纽或主干道等特定区域。

cues.en: I rarely hear about bringing back low impact commercial spaces like restaurants, cafes, and retail shops into existing residential neighborhoods.
cues.zh: 我很少听到有人提议把低影响的商业空间（如餐馆、咖啡馆和零售店）重新引入现有的住宅区。

cues.en: And far too much of the area in North American cities is still zoned as exclusively r one single family homes.
cues.zh: 而且，北美城市中绝大部分面积仍然被划为单一的 R1 独栋住宅区。

cues.en: In Toronto for example, this is called the Yellow Belt because despite Downtown Toronto being one of the most urbanized areas in North America,
cues.zh: 以多伦多为例，这被称为“黄带”（Yellow Belt），因为尽管多伦多市中心是北美城市化程度最高的地区之一，

cues.en: it is still surrounded by a sea of yellow on zoning maps where only single family homes can be built.
cues.zh: 但在分区地图上，它仍然被一片黄色的海洋所包围，这里只能建造独栋住宅。

cues.en: So I'm happy to live again in a place with sane zoning laws that allow beautiful urban environments like this to exist.
cues.zh: 所以我很高兴能再次生活在一个拥有合理分区法的地方，这里允许像这样美丽的城市环境存在。

cues.en: Places that reduce car traffic, support local entrepreneurs,
cues.zh: 这些地方能够减少汽车交通、支持本土创业者、

cues.en: encourage diverse retail, and promote walkability.
cues.zh: 促进多元零售，并提升步行友好度。

cues.en: Because honestly, I have absolutely no interest in going back to live in a place like this.
cues.zh: 因为说实话，我绝对没有兴趣再回到那样的地方去生活。

cues.en: And speaking of supporting small businesses, I've had several people ask if they can contribute to the future of not just bikes. So last week I set up a Patreon account.
cues.zh: 说到支持小企业，有几个人问过是否可以为 Not Just Bikes 的未来出一份力。所以上周我开通了一个 Patreon 账号。

cues.en: If you'd like to support the channel, check out patreon.com/notjustbikes
cues.zh: 如果你想支持本频道，请访问 patreon.com/notjustbikes

cues.en: or click on the link below.
cues.zh: 或者点击下方的链接。

cues.en: As for me, I've got to get some milk. I may not be able to buy it in bags anymore, but at least I can walk there.
cues.zh: 至于我，我得去买点牛奶。虽然我可能买不到袋装牛奶了，但至少我可以走着去。
